name: Historical Centre of the City of Yaroslavl
description: Yaroslavl sits where the Kotorosl River meets the Volga, about 250 km north-east of Moscow, and is one of the cities of Russia's Golden Ring. Its centre is known for richly decorated 17th-century churches, set among neoclassical streets laid out in a fan-shaped plan ordered by Catherine the Great in 1763. The fortress-like Spassky Monastery, founded in the late 12th century, rises above the riverbank.
